title: Data center site selection: the US permitting work to do before committing
description: A US due diligence guide to data center siting, zoning, utility service, environmental permits, and the evidence to collect before committing to a site.
intro: Before committing to a data center site, ask the project team to produce two drawings: the campus it wants to build and the infrastructure needed to make that campus work. Put the generator yard, substation, cooling equipment, water connections, access roads, and transmission route on them. Then ask which approvals cover each element. A parcel can look ready in a land presentation while the route to an operating facility remains unresolved.
takeaways: Compare sites against one consistent campus design, including later phases and off-site infrastructure.
Keep land-use permission, utility service commitments, and environmental authorizations as separate decisions.
Attach a document, accountable owner, and unresolved condition to every claimed approval.
Refresh the assessment when load, cooling, generation, layout, or ownership changes.

sections.heading: Define the project before comparing parcels

blocks.text: A useful comparison starts with a common design brief. State the initial and ultimate electrical demand, load ramp, building area, cooling approach, generator count, fuel storage, and commissioning strategy. Distinguish IT load from total facility load. Mark what is fixed, what is an estimate, and what could change with a tenant commitment. Otherwise, one site will appear easier simply because its assessment assumes a smaller or less demanding facility.

Give the brief a revision number and use it in every preliminary meeting. The utility, planning department, civil engineer, and air consultant should be evaluating the same project. Ask each reviewer to identify the assumptions that would require a new review. A useful answer is specific: an additional generator row, a relocated substation, a different discharge destination, or a larger second phase.

Treat the developable area as an engineering conclusion to be demonstrated. On the concept plan, reserve space for the infrastructure, access, screening, drainage, and setbacks identified during review. Record which constraints can be designed around and which would defeat the intended campus capacity.

sections.heading: Separate a power conversation from a power commitment

blocks.text: Dominion Energy's Virginia data center process illustrates the distinction. Its team can evaluate prospective sites and provide a preliminary power plan. Moving toward service involves a site plan, load letter, load ramp, infrastructure design, rights of way, permitting, and, where required, regulatory filings. Dominion also describes staged service while the final power plan is built. Those are distinct milestones, not a single confirmation that full capacity is available.

For each candidate, request a written record of the proposed service voltage, initial energization capacity, ultimate capacity, enabling projects, customer obligations, and assumptions behind the date. Identify the stage of each response: preliminary feasibility, completed study, proposed agreement, executed agreement, or infrastructure under construction. Read a will-serve letter for its actual conditions rather than treating its title as a delivery guarantee.

Make the dependency visible when off-site work is involved. Who controls the substation parcel? Who obtains the necessary easements? Which approvals belong to the utility, and which belong to the developer? What happens to commissioning if staged service supports only part of the planned load? The answer should change the development schedule, procurement plan, or financing assumption.

sections.heading: Compare the decision gates, not a state's reputation

blocks.text: These examples show different questions a real site assessment must answer. They are not a ranking of jurisdictions or a substitute for parcel-specific advice. Local ordinances, previously approved plans, utility territories, and the proposed generation configuration can change the applicable path.

rows: Loudoun County, Virginia

The March 2025 zoning changes moved data centers from by-right treatment to conditional or special-exception treatment in affected areas. A separate grandfathering resolution addresses certain earlier applications.
Current zoning classification, application history, and a documented conclusion about whether a Special Exception is required.
Fairfax County, Virginia
For projects subject to the adopted data center standards, a noise study is required before site-plan approval and a post-construction study before the Nonresidential Use Permit.
Acoustic design assumptions, equipment layout, study scope, and responsibility for the completed facility's verification.
AEP Ohio service territory
The utility requires an application for new data centers and expansions. Applicable larger requests proceed through load studies and service contracts under its Data Center Tariff.
The applicable tariff, study status, proposed service plan, contract conditions, and infrastructure dependencies.
California
The California Energy Commission has jurisdiction over certain associated power-generation facilities. Its Small Power Plant Exemption process does not remove the need for the remaining permits.
Generation-jurisdiction analysis, environmental-review lead, and the relationship between CEC, local land-use, and air-district decisions.

blocks.text: Loudoun is also reviewing a second phase of data center and substation standards. Separate the rules already adopted from changes still under consideration. Record the date of your zoning analysis and the documents supporting any reliance on an earlier approval. The county explicitly says its application-pathway guide is illustrative and that the ordinance and adopted grandfathering resolution control.

For an Ohio comparison, do not apply AEP Ohio's process to every parcel in the state. Confirm the serving utility first. AEP's published process distinguishes a study from an executed service agreement and describes an estimated energization date with infrastructure-related contingencies. That distinction belongs in the investment memo.

sections.heading: Run environmental screening before the layout becomes expensive to change

blocks.text: Start with the proposed work, not just the parcel boundary. Access roads, utility corridors, outfalls, and temporary construction areas can create separate impacts. The Corps' Section 404 program addresses discharges of dredged or fill material into waters of the United States, including jurisdictional wetlands. Have the relevant aquatic resources investigated and the regulatory path confirmed before relying on a desktop map or assuming that work outside the main building footprint is immaterial.

Construction stormwater is a different authorization. EPA identifies discharges from construction disturbing one acre or more, including smaller disturbances that are part of a qualifying larger common plan. Identify the permitting authority and the applicable permit, then coordinate coverage with grading and erosion controls. A phased campus should be assessed as a development plan, not as a collection of unrelated work orders.

Bring the generator layout into site selection early. New Source Review includes major-source and minor-source permitting programs, generally administered by state or local air agencies. Applicability and permit conditions can affect the generation configuration and operating plan. A familiar engine model does not answer the site-specific permitting question.

Water infrastructure has its own approval path. For example, Loudoun Water requires approved construction drawings and its construction permit before work affecting existing or proposed water, sewer, or reclaimed-water infrastructure, including relevant grading. Its process can also require easements and flow or reclaimed-water agreements. Put these tasks on the same schedule as the civil works they enable.

sections.heading: Turn the permit list into a sequence of decisions

blocks.text: A list that says zoning, air, water, building, and power is too coarse to manage. For each approval, record its issuing authority, prerequisite design inputs, required studies, public-review steps if applicable, conditions, and the activity it authorizes. Keep pending applications separate from issued permits. Ask the responsible specialist to identify the actual release point for the next package of work.

items: Before land commitment: resolve the fatal constraints, define the remaining investigations, and align the contract milestones with those unresolved decisions.
Before equipment commitment: check the proposed engines, cooling system, and substation arrangement against the design used for the applications.
Before construction release: identify the precise work package and document which permissions allow it to proceed.
Before commissioning: reconcile permitted operating conditions with load-bank testing, phased power delivery, water use, and the intended occupancy sequence.

blocks.text: Track changes through their consequences. If acoustic mitigation moves a generator enclosure, reopen the relevant layout, air, access, and civil assumptions. If the utility changes the service route, reassess the corridor rather than leaving the environmental review attached only to the original campus drawing. Assign one person to maintain the common design record.

sections.heading: What the investment decision should contain

blocks.text: A decision-ready site record should explain what can be built, what can be powered, what remains conditional, and who can resolve each condition. Include the current concept plan, utility correspondence, entitlement analysis, environmental findings, approval register, and a schedule tied to those documents. Use a short list of unresolved decisions with costs or schedule consequences where the team has evidence to estimate them.

The strongest site is not necessarily the one with the fewest applications. It is the one whose remaining decisions are understood well enough to support the proposed commitment. Keep that record alive through procurement and commissioning. Its value disappears if the facility changes while the approval assumptions stay frozen.

faqs.question: Does industrial zoning mean a data center can be built by right?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Read the jurisdiction's use classification, use-specific standards, and any conditions affecting the parcel. Loudoun's changes and Fairfax's adopted standards show why an industrial label alone is insufficient.

faqs.question: Is a utility will-serve letter enough to confirm the opening date?
faqs.answer: Read its scope and conditions. A preliminary service statement is different from a studied power plan and executed agreements covering the proposed load ramp. Dominion lists several infrastructure and approval steps between site evaluation and delivery.

faqs.question: Can permitting and utility planning proceed in parallel?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. Dominion explicitly identifies opportunities for concurrent work. Manage the interfaces so a revised load, layout, or service route reaches every team whose submission depends on it.

faqs.question: How long does data center permitting take in the United States?
faqs.answer: There is no dependable national duration. Establish the required approvals and infrastructure first, then build a schedule from the project's actual studies, review steps, and unresolved conditions. A published utility study target is not an operating date.

title: Data center backup generators: how to plan the air-permit path
description: A practical US guide to generator-fleet air permitting, emergency-use restrictions, federal engine standards, source aggregation, and operating records.
intro: Before ordering a generator fleet, settle what the engines will do. Emergency backup, commissioning, routine testing, grid support, and temporary power before utility service are different operating scenarios. Put each on the design brief. The permitting team needs to assess the equipment against that operating plan, and the operations team needs a record it can use when somebody asks to run the fleet.
takeaways: Evaluate the individual engines, the combined stationary source, and the intended operating modes.
Keep federal engine standards separate from site-specific construction and operating permits.
Do not turn a limited local-reliability provision into a blanket demand-response allowance.
Match procurement specifications, permit calculations, and operating records to the same equipment register.

sections.heading: Three assessments are needed before procurement

blocks.text: First, identify the federal standards for each engine. EPA's framework distinguishes compression ignition, typically diesel, from spark ignition; new from existing engines; and major from area sources of hazardous air pollutants. The principal rules are NSPS Subpart IIII, NSPS Subpart JJJJ, and the RICE NESHAP in Subpart ZZZZ. Applicability depends on the engine and source facts, not the label on the building.

Second, determine the site's New Source Review path. EPA identifies Prevention of Significant Deterioration, nonattainment NSR, and minor-source permitting. A facility may have obligations under more than one part of this framework. Most permits are issued by state or local air agencies, whose approved programs have their own requirements and procedures.

Third, assess operating-permit applicability, including Title V. EPA bases major-source status on actual or potential emissions, with pollutant-specific thresholds and lower thresholds in some nonattainment areas. A minor construction-permit conclusion does not, by itself, finish this separate assessment. Record the basis for each conclusion.

sections.heading: Build one equipment register for the entire campus

blocks.text: Start the inventory with every proposed engine, including the fire pump, temporary units, and later phases. Record fuel, manufacturer, model, engine family, rated output, relevant manufacture and construction dates, emission data, control equipment, location, and intended use. Separate unknown specifications from verified vendor information. Reconcile the inventory to the electrical single-line diagram and the site plan.

Then define the stationary source. Separate contracts, buildings, phases, or corporate entities are not a sufficient basis for assuming separate air-permit treatment. Virginia DEQ's data center guidance addresses adjacency and common ownership, declines to give a distance that will resolve every case, and notes that changes to boundaries or ownership can require reconsideration. Obtain the applicable source determination rather than designing around a guessed separation.

Evaluate potential emissions using the accepted methodology for the relevant program. Expected annual testing hours are not automatically a legal restriction on potential to emit. EPA's guidance distinguishes equipment capability from enforceable limits on how equipment may operate. If the permit strategy relies on a restriction, define the limit and the records that will make it demonstrable.

Stress-test the proposed limits against the actual operating plan. Include commissioning, scheduled tests, maintenance recovery, and the plausible combinations of engines running together. Ask what happens when a replacement unit arrives or a second phase opens. The objective is a permit basis the facility can live within, not simply an emissions spreadsheet that clears the first review.

sections.heading: Give each operating mode a separate decision

blocks.text: Emergency classification includes restrictions on operation. Do not treat every interruption risk, commercial dispatch request, or delay to utility service as an emergency. EPA's 2025 backup-generator interpretation describes limited local-reliability provisions with specific eligibility conditions. It does not authorize unrestricted revenue-generating operation by every emergency engine.

rows: Actual emergency
Does the event meet the applicable rule and permit definition? Which conditions continue to apply?
Event description, supporting outage or incident record, engine IDs, start and stop times.
Maintenance and readiness testing
Which hour limits, test purposes, and permit conditions apply to this engine?
Test reason, authorizing maintenance instruction, duration, load, and cumulative hours.
Commissioning and load-bank testing
Has the proposed sequence been included in the permit basis, and how is each run classified?
Approved test plan, expected engine combinations, calculations, and the resulting operating log.
Local grid reliability or demand response
Does the particular program and engine satisfy a current authorized provision, and does the site permit allow it?
Program terms, applicability review, dispatch instruction, and required event records.
Bridge or routine site power
Does the proposed use require a non-emergency permitting and emissions basis?
A separately reviewed operating scenario before committing to this power strategy.

blocks.text: Keep the table with the operating procedure. Dispatch authority should be clear, especially where a utility or third party can request operation. A site engineer should not have to reconstruct the permit interpretation during a power event. Translate the approved decision into the control room's instructions and escalation contacts.

sections.heading: State requirements can change the equipment you buy

blocks.text: Virginia now provides a concrete procurement example. Code § 10.1-1322.6 applies to data center air-permit applications submitted on or after July 1, 2026, including general-permit coverage. It requires the permitted emission limit for each generator set to be no greater than emissions achieved by a Tier 4-equivalent set. The law defines that equivalence through specified pollution-control systems or their equivalents and preserves DEQ's ability to impose stricter limits.

For an affected Virginia application, verify that the proposed package can demonstrate the required emissions performance in its permitted configuration. Do not rely on an equipment brochure's use of a tier label. Obtain the emissions data, control description, operating assumptions, and supplier commitments needed by the air-permit team. Check the application date and the scope of any proposed modification with DEQ.

The Bay Area Air District's engine application illustrates another layer of site-specific work. It requests engine specifications, fuel consumption, pollutant emission rates, and a health-risk-assessment form for diesel engines. The application also distinguishes circumstances involving nearby schools and overburdened communities. The package required for a California location is not established by showing that the same engine was accepted elsewhere.

Preserve the design inputs behind the air analysis. If a vendor changes stack geometry, exhaust characteristics, or the control package, send the revision back to the permit team. If the civil layout changes, check whether the submitted locations and nearby receptors still match. These are design-control tasks, not items to defer until the equipment reaches the site.

sections.heading: An engine certificate does not close the permit file

blocks.text: EPA describes a certification-based compliance approach for many stationary engines that also requires installation, configuration, operation, and maintenance according to the manufacturer's instructions. Other engine categories have different demonstration requirements. Keep the certificate or applicable emissions demonstration with the actual model and configuration being procured.

A federal engine-compliance route and permission to construct or operate the source address different questions. NSR permits specify authorized construction, emission limits, and often operating conditions. Confirm the applicable construction restriction with the permitting authority before releasing a work package. Do not infer either that all site work must stop or that a building permit authorizes generator installation.

Rental equipment deserves the same attention. EPA notes that a portable nonroad engine can become stationary after remaining in one location for more than twelve months, with a separate rule for seasonal sources. Wheels or a rental agreement do not settle the classification. Review the planned placement, duration, replacements, and operating purpose before treating temporary generation as outside the air-permit plan.

sections.heading: Hand over a usable operating record

blocks.text: The final handover should connect each engine to its applicable requirements, allowed operating modes, limits, maintenance instructions, and reporting duties. EPA's engine compliance summaries identify different combinations of monitoring, maintenance, notifications, testing, and records by engine category. Assign the obligations from the actual rules and permit rather than using the same generic checklist for every unit.

items: Reconcile installed serial numbers, engine families, controls, and locations against the approved equipment register.
Make each limit readable: what is measured, which engines it covers, its averaging period, and who checks the remaining allowance.
Record runs by purpose as well as duration, with evidence supporting emergency or local-reliability classification.
Assign ownership of maintenance records, emissions-test results, notifications, and required reports.
Require a documented review before changing fuel, controls, engine count, placement, or dispatch arrangements.

blocks.text: The fleet will eventually face a request the original design meeting did not anticipate. A good compliance record makes the answer traceable. It shows what was approved, which assumptions supported that approval, and what must be reassessed before the operating plan changes.

faqs.question: Are emergency data center generators exempt from air permits?
faqs.answer: Not as a general rule. Emergency status changes some engine requirements, but federal standards and state or local air-permitting requirements must still be assessed separately. A permitting exemption under one program does not establish an exemption under every other program.

faqs.question: Can backup generators earn demand-response revenue?
faqs.answer: Only where the engine, program, operation, and permit satisfy the relevant requirements. EPA's 2025 interpretation concerns specific local-reliability provisions. Obtain a documented determination for the proposed arrangement before treating it as an allowed operating mode.

faqs.question: Does an EPA-certified engine guarantee that the site will receive an air permit?
faqs.answer: No. Certification can support the engine's federal compliance demonstration. Site permitting still evaluates the applicable source, emissions, operating conditions, and local requirements.

faqs.question: Should later generator phases be included in the initial assessment?
faqs.answer: Show the permitting team the planned buildout and explain its timing. The appropriate application scope and source determination depend on the applicable program and project facts. Include foreseeable phases so procurement and future modifications use consistent assumptions.

title: Data center water and stormwater permits: resolve each flow before construction
description: A US guide to data center water supply, wastewater discharge, construction and industrial stormwater, oil storage, and wetlands permitting dependencies.
intro: Start with a water balance and a drainage drawing. Show where each stream comes from, what changes its quality, where it goes, and who controls that destination. Include cooling, sanitation, equipment flushing, construction dewatering, rainfall, and spills. A water-service agreement answers a supply question. It does not establish that every resulting discharge is acceptable.
takeaways: Confirm supply and discharge arrangements separately, including temporary construction and commissioning flows.
Determine construction and industrial stormwater applicability independently. A facility's name does not settle its operating classification.
Screen the whole development footprint, including off-site connections, for water and wetland impacts.
Carry approved flow, chemistry, drainage, and fuel-storage assumptions into the operating team's procedures.

sections.heading: Start with supply capacity and the actual discharge route

blocks.text: Ask the water provider to evaluate initial and ultimate demand, peak conditions, fire protection, connection points, and any reclaimed-water proposal. Record which infrastructure must exist before each phase can receive service. If the project proposes its own surface-water withdrawal, investigate that separate authorization: Virginia, for example, administers a surface-water withdrawal permitting program through DEQ.

Utility infrastructure has its own approval sequence. Loudoun Water requires approved drawings and a construction permit before work affecting its existing or proposed water, sanitary-sewer, or reclaimed-water infrastructure, including relevant grading. Its process can also require easements, estimated-flow acknowledgments, reclaimed-water allocation agreements, and process-wastewater metering arrangements.

Next, trace the outgoing water. A pollutant discharge from a point source to waters of the United States requires NPDES authorization. A discharge to a municipal sanitary sewer instead raises the receiving utility's requirements and applicable pretreatment obligations. A storm drain is a different destination again; do not assume it is an acceptable route for cooling or commissioning wastewater.

Send the receiving authority a discharge profile, not just an annual consumption estimate: flow, temperature, expected constituents, treatment chemicals, frequency, and any concentrated or intermittent releases. Those facts let the authority evaluate the proposed stream and identify missing information. Keep the response with the cooling-system design revision it evaluated.

sections.heading: Build the approval matrix around individual streams

rows: Potable or reclaimed supply
What service and infrastructure approvals apply to this phase?
Provider response, demand basis, connection design, easements, allocation conditions.
Cooling blowdown or equipment flushing
Will the sewer authority accept this composition and flow, and under what conditions?
Discharge profile, treatment-chemical information, sampling and metering requirements.
Direct wastewater outfall
Which NPDES authority and authorization cover this discharge?
Outfall location, receiving water, pollutant profile, permit conditions.
Construction runoff or dewatering
Which construction coverage and discharge conditions fit the work and destination?
Disturbance plan, drainage routes, controls, authorization and inspection responsibilities.
Operating stormwater
Do the actual industrial activities and state rules require coverage?
Classification analysis, material-exposure inventory, drainage map, authority response.
Oil storage and handling
Does SPCC apply, and how will releases be contained and managed?
Container-capacity inventory, drainage review, applicable spill-prevention plan.

blocks.text: Temporary work deserves a row of its own. San José's industrial wastewater program, for example, provides short-term authorizations for activities including construction dewatering to the sanitary sewer. Resolve the local path before a contractor chooses a discharge point. A future operating arrangement is not evidence that today's temporary discharge has been reviewed.

sections.heading: Distinguish construction runoff from operating stormwater

blocks.text: Under the federal construction-stormwater framework, stormwater discharges from activities disturbing at least one acre generally require permit coverage. Smaller disturbances also qualify when part of a common plan that ultimately disturbs at least one acre. Clearing, grading, and excavation count. Identify the state or EPA permitting authority and the applicable permit before relying on a generic construction checklist.

Use the permit to assign responsibility for the pollution-prevention plan, installed controls, inspections, corrective work, and records. Check how its conditions address construction dewatering and stabilization. Put those responsibilities into the contractor's scope, and identify who keeps the evidence if the general contractor or site operator changes.

Operating industrial-stormwater coverage is a separate applicability decision. EPA's federal framework identifies regulated categories of industrial activity; state programs administer most coverage and must be checked for their requirements. Assess the facility's actual activities and relevant classification. Neither a data-center label nor the existence of a fuel tank alone answers every industrial-stormwater question.

There is a specific September 2026 issue in EPA-administered areas: EPA's 2021 Multi-Sector General Permit expired on February 28, 2026. Previously covered operators retain administratively continued coverage and obligations. New facilities and new operators cannot obtain coverage under that expired permit. EPA describes a conditional No Action Assurance for certain eligible operators, but explicitly says it does not confer NPDES permit coverage. Confirm the available path with the responsible EPA office. This federal permit status is not the status of every state's general permit.

sections.heading: Screen the connections as well as the campus

blocks.text: A workable building footprint can still depend on a road, water line, or power connection crossing an aquatic feature. Section 404 regulates discharges of dredged or fill material into waters of the United States, including jurisdictional wetlands. Include temporary construction impacts in the review. A map flag should prompt investigation; it does not establish either federal jurisdiction or permission to proceed.

Where an activity requiring a federal permit or license may result in a discharge into waters of the United States, Clean Water Act Section 401 can add a state or authorized tribal water-quality certification decision. The applicable certification must be obtained or waived before the federal authorization can issue. Review state water requirements separately as well. These reviews are related, but a construction-stormwater authorization does not resolve a fill-permit question.

Keep alternative connection routes on the table until the impacts are understood. Show the environmental reviewer the grading limits, access works, staging areas, and utility corridors, not only the finished campus rendering.

sections.heading: Check fuel storage against drainage and spill requirements

blocks.text: For SPCC applicability, EPA asks whether a non-transportation-related facility handles oil and could reasonably discharge harmful quantities to navigable waters or adjoining shorelines. One capacity trigger is aggregate aboveground oil storage greater than 1,320 US gallons, counting containers of 55 gallons or more subject to the rule's exclusions. A separate test addresses completely buried storage. Evaluate capacity, not just today's tank contents.

Reconcile the storage inventory with the generator plan and site drainage. For a facility subject to SPCC, translate its plan into physical controls and operating responsibilities. Keep fuel delivery, containment inspection, spill response, and changes in storage configuration visible in the handover. A spill-prevention plan does not serve as wastewater-discharge authorization.

sections.heading: Hand over the approved assumptions, not just the drawings

blocks.text: Before commissioning, assemble a stream-by-stream record: destination, approval or documented applicability conclusion, limits, sampling point, reporting owner, and the design assumptions behind it. Include one-time flushing and testing. Mark unresolved conditions clearly so an issued document is not mistaken for completion of every prerequisite.

Then define the changes that reopen review: cooling technology, treatment chemicals, discharge flow, drainage connections, site expansion, and oil-storage capacity. Industrial users have applicable notification duties for changed discharges and other specified events. The operating team needs to recognize those triggers before making the change.

faqs.question: Does a water-service commitment authorize cooling wastewater discharge?
faqs.answer: No. Confirm the discharge destination and its applicable requirements separately. The sewer authority evaluates an indirect discharge; a qualifying direct discharge requires NPDES authorization. Keep the supply and discharge decisions in separate records.

faqs.question: Does every US data center need an industrial-stormwater permit?
faqs.answer: Do not infer applicability from the facility name. Evaluate its activities against the applicable industrial categories and the responsible state's or EPA's program. Construction-stormwater requirements need a separate assessment.

faqs.question: Does an air-cooled design eliminate water-related permitting?
faqs.answer: It changes the cooling-water assumptions. It does not answer questions about construction runoff, sanitary service, oil storage, or work affecting jurisdictional waters. Rebuild the approval matrix for the actual design rather than carrying over a cooling-specific conclusion.
